correctness.rationale: For any zero-annihilator evolution algebra of rank-one square, the multiplication is a nondegenerate diagonalizable symmetric bilinear form times a nonzero product generator. The characteristic-two Frobenius automorphism uniquely normalizes each natural basis to an orthonormal frame. The characteristic vector t is fixed by every dot-product isometry; a direct symplectic decomposition establishes complete odd/even isometry groups and their orbits on the generator. A nonzero-coordinate-sum recursion gives exact Hamming frequencies, and free reordering of frames gives C_k=G_d H_k/(d! T). The group order and orbit decomposition are proved symbolically for all q=2^e (e>=2) and d>=2. Finite exhaustive checks with a standalone standard-library verifier were run for q=2,4,8 and dimensions up to five (q=2 is an excluded boundary test), covering every claimed orbit case. The included verifier also checks every nonzero product vector over F4 in dimensions three and four and over F8 in dimension three (63, 255 and 511 vectors respectively).

originality.rationale: The October 15, 2026 survey arXiv:2610.22248v1 raises questions about counting natural bases and graph variability but gives neither the complete q>=4 characteristic-two rank-one graph-support spectrum nor the exact multiplicity C_k. The 2025 open-access one-dimensional-square paper classifies algebras via bilinear forms and isometries, without the support-frequency enumeration of natural bases. The 2020 natural-families full PDF gives basis-change structure but not the extension-field graph census. Comparison to recorded results restricted to F2 and odd characteristic finds disjoint field domains, not a direct implication. Indexed mathematical-record searches returned no matching statement; unindexed orthogonal-frame enumerations remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: Standard symplectic orbit and finite-field Hamming-count formulas might have been combined previously in an unindexed orthogonal-frame enumeration.

value.rationale: A natural complete classification of basis-graph variability and exact multiplicities for every rank-one nondegenerate evolution algebra over F_{2^e}, e>=2, and every d>=2. It provides explicit closed counts of a motivated natural algebraic invariant (equivalence classes of natural bases and directed graphs), and describes the sharp extension-field expansion of attainable support graphs beyond the F2 parity restrictions. It directly addresses the class-specific part of explicit open natural-basis and graph-dependence questions. No arbitrary parameter slice, mere normalization check, or claim to classify general evolution algebras is needed.
